top.title: Christian persecution in Nigeria worrisome — Catholic bishops
top.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. In his address, Archbishop Ugorji said the human and material consequences of the country’s insecurity remained alarming, irrespective of whether the crisis was viewed as targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict. “Ultimately, whether the crisis is perceived as a targeted persecution of Christians or a complex socio-economic conflict, the human and material toll is undeniable. “It is deeply troubling that tens of thousands have lost their lives, millions remain internally displaced, the education of thousands of children is truncated, and millions of naira have been lost through destruction of property and paying ransom,” he said. top.title: Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo
top.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.” On security in the state, Governor Okpebholo said his administration took stiff measures to reduce the level of killings and kidnapping in the state. Some of the measures, he said, was destroying any building that was linked to kidnapping and cult related activities in the state irrespective of the social status of the person involved. He said: “These are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us. To be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights. Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night. “In the next few weeks, it will be safer because there will be police at every corner of the state to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. Whether you take a bush path, they will follow you up.” The post Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Back on top: Christian Brothers Academy football blasts Saratoga Springs in the Class AA Super Bowl
top.description: CBA head coach Bobby Burns gets water dumped on him after his team beat Saratoga for the Section 2, Class AA title on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at Colonie High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - The Redemption Tour reached its Section 2 conclusion Saturday. And what a crescendo it turned out to be for the Christian Brothers Academy football team. One year after getting stunned by one point in the Class AA Super Bowl against Saratoga Springs, the Brothers returned to the same Colonie High School field vs. the same opponent and authored a thorough thrashing in the title-game rematch. CBA scored six touchdowns on six possessions in the first half on its way to throttling the Blue Streaks 61-14. Last year, Saratoga Springs stunned CBA 14-13 for the championship. "Coming into the game, I was so hyped. Scoring that first touchdown just meant so much to me," said CBA senior running back Tommy Toher, who was knocked out of the 2025 title game with an injury in the first quarter, but opened Saturday's scoring on a 25-yard TD run. "The culture, the continuity and the love for each other has been there since last year. They were motivated and focused all offseason," CBA coach Bobby Burns said. "These kids are special. They really are. Yes, we have a lot of talent on this team, but they let us coach them, they trust us, they execute and play their tails off when they need to. Most of all, they have been dedicated to improving since last year. I am proud of them." Saturday's win was especially sweet for veteran CBA players who felt the sting of falling to Saratoga Springs in a driving rainstorm in the 2025 Super Bowl. But it also meant a great deal to players that either had minimal roles last year or - as in the case of senior quarterback Matt Kowalski - players who barely hit the field. Kowalski rushed for three touchdowns and passed for two on Saturday, while another one of CBA's standouts was Myles Johnson - a starter at linebacker for two years - who ran for a pair of touchdowns. "It just shows you how good this team is. People like Matt and Myles were the hardest workers of all," said CBA senior standout JT Vogel, a four-year starter at safety. "They showed up ready to work at every workout. I love those guys so much, so I am glad to see them shine." "Guys like Myles and Matt are products of the offseason work. They gained confidence and prepared themselves to do what they have done this year," Burns said. Toward the end of the opening quarter, the Blue Streaks trailed 21-0. Things never got better, as the Brothers outgained Saratoga Springs 462-6. The Blue Streaks' two touchdowns came on a kickoff return from Gavin LaFrance and a 2-yard reception by Jaden Lockrow after the Blue Streaks were set up with a short field. top.title: Watch: Arch Manning connects with Raleek Brown for clutch TD, road upset of LSU
top.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) celebrates a touchdown during the game against LSU at Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Arch Manning delivered his most clutch moment yet Saturday night. The Texas football quarterback struggled mightily in the first three quarters at LSU, throwing three interceptions as the Longhorns trailed 21-13 entering the final frame. Manning then rose to the occasion on the game's final drive. And Texas, No. 6 in the College Football Playoff rankings, virtually sealed its spot in the postseason tournament and dashed the hopes of Lane Kiffin and LSU. Here's a look at his game-winning touchdown pass with just 2 seconds left, and the plays that preceded it: How Arch Manning delivered in fourth quarter. Texas needed a touchdown on its final drive in its 22-21 road win. It began the drive on Texas' 42-yard line, and Manning and the Longhorns' then faced a 3rd-and-3 with 1:28 to play. Manning generated a first down on a slant to wide receiver Ryan Wingo. He then added another first-down pass to Wingo, and he added two additional first downs with his legs. The Longhorns' march deep into LSU territory concluded with a second-and-goal at the LSU four-yard line with two seconds remaining. Manning took a shotgun snap, dropped back, then lofted a pass to running back Raleek Brown down the right sideline. Brown hauled in the pass. Texas took the lead, then escaped Baton Rougue with a clutch comeback victory on the subsequent kickoff. Arch Manning and Raleek Brown with the biggest play of their careers. top.title: Texas outlasts LSU thanks to last second heroics by Arch Manning
top.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Texas outlasts LSU thanks to last second heroics by Arch Manning appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas football quarterback Arch Manning received fierce criticism for his turnover marred outing versus LSU . But he pulled off the epic last second heroics with Raleek Brown at Baton Rouge Saturday. The running back Brown caught LSU off guard with his motion to the left. Manning lasered his short throw from inside LSU’s five-yard line for the final touchdown with two seconds left. Texas ultimately held on for the 22-21 victory thanks to a final special teams stop. But again, Manning overcame a multiple interception evening to pull off this epic goal line touchdown. But the Longhorns kept their own hopes alive for both. Texas now joins Alabama and Tennessee as the conference’s remaining eight-win teams with two regular season games left. The Longhorns own the tiebreaker with the latter SEC rival after beating them earlier this season. So the path to both Atlanta come Dec. 5 and the CFP is becoming crystallized for Texas. Manning still needed to shed the memories of his earlier picks. LSU grabbed three Manning passes, with Ty Benefield snatching two of those errant throws and took one back for the touchdown. DJ Pickett grabbed the other pick. Manning even noticeable kept moving his right arm clockwise after appearing to injure himself on a previous play. But he orchestrated one epic long scoring drive. top.title: Islanders, Holmstrom tear through Ducks defense, 6-2
top.description: Anaheim, CA - New York Islanders right wing Simon Holmstrom (92) and center Kyle Palmieri (21) celebrate after a second period goal during a regular season NHL game between the New York Islanders and the Anaheim Ducks at Honda Center on November 14, 2026, in Anaheim, CA. ANAHEIM, Calif. – That lightning hot offensive streak of a week ago papered over plenty of the Anaheim Ducks’ defensive cracks, which have suddenly morphed into canyons as the goals have dried up. The New York Islanders scored four in the second period through a porous Ducks defense, and Simon Holmström finished off a hat trick past Lukáš Dostál, as Anaheim was cratered, 6-2, on Saturday at Honda Center. Anaheim (10-9-1, 21 points) has scored just four goals in back-to-back losses after scoring 26 goals in a five-game winning streak and five or more goals in eight straight games. Nikita Nesterenko chased down a loose puck in front for the Ducks’ opening goal in the second period, 2-1, and Cutter Gauthier continued his historic goal-scoring streak later in the middle frame. Gauthier carved out space alone in front, and Tristan Luneau sent in the hard feed for the deflection, 5-2. Gauthier tied 1998-99 Teemu Selanne for the second-longest goal-scoring streak in franchise history. Selanne also owns the longest streak in team history at 11 games (1997-98). Ben Hutton was the beneficiary of a double deflection off Ducks sticks just under two minutes into the game, but the Islanders were off to the race in the second period, as wheels came off for Anaheim’s defense. Bo Horvat netted a one-timer six seconds into the first power play of the game, 2-0. Simon Holmstrom scored his first of two 25 seconds after the Ducks’ first goal from Nesterenko, as he finished a two-on-one with Matthew Schaefer. Holmstrom scored a second five minutes later, as Dostál was slid into by Leo Carlsson, and Mitchell Chaffee put in the Islanders’ fifth, as Schaefer flew the zone for another two-on-one. Holmstrom finished off the hat trick with a one-on-one beat of Dostál’s glove in the third period, 6-2. Lukáš Dostál stopped 19 of 25 shots in his first start in over a week, when he was pulled after the first period in Calgary last Friday. Ville Husso was the back-up, as Laurent Brossoit was reassigned back to AHL San Diego yesterday. Brossoit–who won his first four starts of the five he made with the Ducks during their red hot offensive streak–was the only goalie waiver exempt, and thus he was not at risk for a claim by another team when being sent to the minors. Semyon Varlamov made 26 saves for the Islanders. Anaheim concludes its four-game homestand with the second half of a back-to-back against the Calgary Flames on Sunday before hitting the road for a four-game trip, which begins in St. Louis on Tuesday.

top.title: Steve Sarkisian dials up game-winning TD pass to Raleek Brown
top.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Running back Raleek Brown #0 of the Texas Longhorns celebrates his touchdown during the game between Louisiana State Tigers and Texas Longhorns at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Aric Becker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images In high-profile calls on the goal line over the last several seasons, Steve Sarkisian has come up short in tenure-defining moments. On Saturday in Baton Rouge, facing off against longtime friend and former colleague Lane Kiffin, Sarkisian faced a season-defining moment hoping to make a better call than he has in the past with six seconds remaining and Texas trailing 21-16 at the LSU 4-yard line. With no timeouts remaining, the Longhorns had no more than two plays remaining. After LSU took away some of the play calls that Sarkisian went back to over the previous two games, a condensed formation created leverage to the field with return motion from running back Raleek Brown creating a clear pre-snap picture for Arch Manning. Trying to match up with Brown in coverage, LSU linebacker Davohn Keys was slow to respond to the return motion, had to take a wide angle around the field corner, and got torched, allowing Manning to hit a one-step drop and drop an easy pass into Brown’s chest for the go-ahead, four-yard touchdown with four seconds remaining. GIVE SARKISIAN HIS CREDIT RALEEK BROWN 1 ON 1 SCORES THE LIKELY GAME-WINNING TD pic.twitter.com/tpBW0Monsp — Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 15, 2026 The Tigers were able to take away Brown in the passing game before the final offensive play for the Horns — Brown only had three catches for four yards on his first four targets, but pitting his speed to the pylon against a slower linebacker who had to navigate traffic ultimately represented one of Sarkisian’s best goal-line play calls in his nearly six years leading the Longhorns. Manning ran to embrace the head coach who trusted him in his lowest moment as an athlete, but it wasn’t a moment to celebrate for the Texas head coach. Up 22-21, Sarkisian had to call a kneel down instead of attempting a point after the Tigers could return for a go-ahead score, and the Longhorns secured the victory on the ensuing kickoff. Reflecting on the play, Brown knew it was won before the snap when a defender didn’t follow him in motion . “I was just real happy,” Brown said . ”Whatever it takes to win.” For Texas, that’s required effective play calls from Sarkisian on the goal line in defining moments. On Saturday, he got it right with one of the single best decisions in his Longhorns tenure.

top.title: MSU football grades for the Spartans' performance against Washington
top.description: Lansing State Journal columnist Graham Couch grades Michigan State's football team after its 21-14 loss to Washington on a scale of 1-10. OFFENSE: 3 This grade should probably be an incomplete. Because MSU’s offense was doing well enough before quarterback Alessio Milivojevic went down in the second quarter with an injury. He was 7-for-12 passing for 108 yards and led a touchdown drive to open the game, which including a 30-yard pass to Bryson Williams and a 26-yard completion to Carson Gulker. Without Milivojevic, MSU had some moments offensively with backup Cam Fancher — including a fourth-down touchdown pass to Williams — but also had some moments Fancher and the Spartans would like to have back, including when he threw an interception as he tried to throw away a pass, also injuring himself on the play as he tried to twist out of a tackle. MSU ran the ball somewhat effectively, with Brandon Tullis carrying 21 times again for 82 yards. And, overall, out-gained Washington 342 yards to 332. There were times when this was an effective offense, especially with Milivojevic under center. But the penalties, inconsistencies and turnovers left the Spartans sitting at 14 points, which wasn’t enough. DEFENSE: 7 Once MSU’s defense got a handle on Washington, that was it for the Huskies for a long time. Early on, the Spartans looked like they might get gashed all night by quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and receiver Chris Lawson. But after the Huskies’ second touchdown, MSU’s defense pressured Williams and largely contained everything Washington tried to do, holding the Huskies to 41 total yards on their first four second-half drives. The Spartans only recorded one sack — Williams is elusive and good as stepping up and through pressure to gain a couple yards — but if you watched the game, you saw the work that was being done to corral him. Washington also was only able to rush for 44 yards on 22 carries. In the end, MSU’s defense needed at least one more stop and gave up a few plays on the final drive that beat them. But this was a strong effort — and could have been a winning effort. This grade would be even better if not for those two early drives and for Kenny Soares Jr.'s roughing the passer penalty, which let Washington’s first drive continue, ending in a touchdown. This might have been a different game without that drive. SPECIAL TEAMS: 5 Liam Boyd missed his only field goal attempt, wide right from 50 yards out, and that might have been costly. He definitely could have given the Spartans the lead early in the fourth quarter with that kick. Rhys Dakin’s punting average, 39.6, was impacted by one kick especially when he was punting with a short field and trying to pin Washington deep. He got it to the 13-yard line. Not a great punt, but decent enough. Overall, he had three punts inside the 20-yard line. And Washington’s return man muffed one of his punts, with the Spartans’ coverage unit jumping on it. Chrishon McCray had one nice, 16-yard punt return.

top.title: ‘Karma’ – Fans react to Lane Kiffin seemingly crying after LSU’s season-ruining loss to Texas
top.description: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin’s emotional moment on the field after their 22-21 loss to the Texas Longhorns ended any hopes of making it to the College Football Playoffs. The Tigers have a 6-4 season record, going 3-4 against the SEC, after the loss to the Longhorns. Kiffin’s first full season in charge of the Tigers after his acrimonious exit from Ole Miss last season has not been a pleasant ride. The emotions of failing to lead a program like LSU to the playoffs in his first full season while continuing the team’s pattern of struggling against top-10 teams left Kiffin overwhelmed after the loss. Lane Kiffin’s tears do not earn him any sympathy from CFB fans With how Kiffin left Ole Miss and his generally boisterous nature in front of the media, fans were clearly rejoicing the apparent tears from the 51-year-old coach in his first season in charge. “The karma finding Lane Kiffin this season is something to behold,” said one seemingly happy fan . “I would cry too if I had to coach Levitt,” were the thoughts of another fan . “Arch Manning had Lane Kiffin crying on the sideline,” joked a fan . “It’s not even the slightest bit difficult (to feel bad for Kiffin) after all of the stunts he’s pulled and people he’s screwed over through the years,” said one fan, rejecting anyone having sympathy for Kiffin . “I like watching him lose… Constant Karma,” said another fan . The tears were justified as this loss was the death sentence for LSU with regard to this season, as even an undefeated season from this point on might not be enough to earn them a spot in the college football playoffs. Kiffin coached Ole Miss to the playoff last season but did not get to see the season through after being asked to leave the program for agreeing midseason to join LSU in 2026, a decision that has kept him more unpopular than ever among casual fans. This is a win for fans with no loyalties, as LSU fans and Kiffin fans will have to wait another year and pray for an improvement. top.description: Beaver Beavers celebrate with the trophy after winning against the Duchesne Eagles during a 1A football state championship held at Eccles Coliseum in Cedar City on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. | Tess Crowley, Deseret News Beaver’s offense was in a brutal hole, down four points near midfield and facing a third down and 21 after taking a bad sack on first down. With less than two minutes remaining Saturday in the 1A state championship game at Southern Utah University, top-ranked Duchesne was two defensive plays away from hoisting its first state championship since in 2021. As Beaver head coach Jon Marshall mulled what play he could possible call on third and long, on his headset he heard assistant coach Ron Echols chime in from the press box, “The waggle screen’s there.” Beaver hadn’t run the play in over two months, and probably because of that Duchesne seemed to caught off by the call. Davis Carter rolled left and then turned around threw it back across the field to Leonardo De Leon, who got two huge blocks to spring him 40 yards down to the 11-yard line. Three plays later, Carter darted into the end zone for the 5-yard go-ahead touchdown with 59 seconds remaining. When teammate Drew Sorensen intercepted a pass on the final play of the game, Beaver players stormed the field to celebrate their 1A state championship win over Duchesne, 22-19. It is the 18th state championship in school history, and third in the past four seasons for the Beavers. top.description: Japan v Brazil - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Legendary former Brazil striker Romario has demanded the immediate dismissal of national team head coach Carlo Ancelotti following Saturday's 3-2 friendly defeat against Japan in Singapore. Taking to social media after the loss, the 1994 World Cup winner urged the Italian tactician to leave his post and return to club management. Iconic striker loses patience completely Romario has called on Brazilian Football Confederation president Samir Xaud to sack Ancelotti before the five-time world champions slide into a deeper crisis. Despite suffering a last-16 elimination against Norway at the 2026 World Cup, the Italian had his contract extended until 2030 . However, Saturday's setback at the Singapore National Stadium prompted the former striker and current Brazilian senator to demand an immediate change in the dugout. Posting on Instagram afterwards, Romario wrote: "Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and get out! Nobody questions your legacy. Federation chief urged to act Although Ancelotti praised his players' comeback and the displays of those handed opportunities , Romario turned his anger towards the federation's leadership to prevent another tournament failure. nigeria.title: Christian persecution in Nigeria worrisome — Catholic bishops
nigeria.description: By Chidi Nkwopara Church leaders have expressed concern over the increasing cases of violent persecution of Christians in parts of Nigeria, saying the disturbing trend has worsened over the past two decades. The Apostolic Nuncio to Nigeria, Archbishop Michael Francis Crotty, and the Archbishop of Owerri, Most Rev. Lucius Iwejuru Ugorji, raised the concern at the weekend in Owerri during their respective addresses at the 18th National Conference of the Association of Papal Knights and Medalists in Nigeria (APKMN). In his address, Crotty said Christians had suffered persecution in different forms throughout Nigeria’s history, but noted that violent forms of persecution had become more pronounced in the last two decades. “In the history of Nigeria, Christians have suffered persecution in different forms, and this disturbing phenomenon has increased within the last two decades, especially the violent forms of persecution. “In recent years, Christians have been targeted by kidnappers, and many lay faithful and priests have been kidnapped. “Many of those kidnapped were killed, and others were released after ransoms were paid. Thousands of churches have been attacked and destroyed since the beginning of Boko Haram and the activities of herdsmen in more recent years,” he said. The Apostolic Nuncio also alleged that Christians in some parts of the country, particularly the North and North-Central regions, had been denied legitimate access to land for the construction of places of worship. “Very often the issue of persecution of Christians in Nigeria is politicised and approached with some sort of bias and religious sentiments. “There is no doubt that people of other faiths have also been affected by insecurity in Nigeria. However, we cannot deny the fact that Christians have been specifically targeted in some parts of the country. “Our concern should be the necessary actions to take in order to bring the unnecessary killing of all citizens to an end, whether they are Christian or of other faiths,” he said. He described the conference theme, “Strategic Engagements in Addressing Christian Persecution in Nigeria: Toward Coordinated Response”, as timely, stressing the need for collective action across religious and community lines. nigeria.title: Why Edo was among first states to approve state police — Okpebholo
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu THE governor of Edo, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has said the state already has the structure for state police to commence and for that reason, the state House of Assembly was one of the first to pass the law as recommended by the National Assembly. Okpebholo spoke in an interview with journalists in Benin-City as part of activities to mark his second year anniversary. “We are prepared. We were one of the first to sign into law, when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo state is safe.” He said his state already has a working security architecture it has tested that could be used to track criminals even outside the state,” he said. Okpebholo said “Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days and as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.” On security in the state, Governor Okpebholo said his administration took stiff measures to reduce the level of killings and kidnapping in the state. Some of the measures, he said, was destroying any building that was linked to kidnapping and cult related activities in the state irrespective of the social status of the person involved. He said: “These are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us. To be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights. Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night. “In the next few weeks, it will be safer because there will be police at every corner of the state to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. nigeria.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. It is practical, it is respectful, and it is necessary for a healthy modern marriage. nigeria.title: Hidden Curriculum of Leadership: What does the environment teach leaders?
nigeria.description: By Dayo Oyinlola Institutions are ecosystems made up of individual units that live in symbiotic relationships with each other. In these environments, information is processed dynamically and learning occurs both formally and informally. We must consider this reality when discussing leadership development. Leaders learn through written documents and institutional codes of conduct: values, laws, behavioral manuals, KPIs and OKRs that organisations establish to hold leaders accountable. And then there are the experiences nobody formally teaches, but everyone learns. A young executive watches how decisions are made. They notice who gets rewarded and who gets overlooked. They observe what happens when someone challenges authority, misses a target, refuses to compromise or asks an uncomfortable question. Nobody necessarily sits them down to teach these lessons. We often think of leadership development as something that happens through formal training, coaching, mentoring and experience. All of these matters, but leaders are also continuously shaped by the systems, institutions, cultures and circumstances within which they operate. And sometimes, the lessons being taught by the environment are very different from the lesson’s organisations believe they are teaching. Consider an organisation that claims to encourage employees to challenge ideas, yet senior leaders consistently dismiss people who disagree with them. Employees then learn that deference is safer than speaking up. Over time, people respond to what they experience rather than what they are told. The environment teaches what is rewarded. It teaches what is tolerated. It teaches how power works, whose voice matters and whether speaking up is valued or punished. It teaches people what leadership really means when it is exercised, not what the organisation says leadership means. This becomes particularly important in difficult operating environments. But there is another question worth asking: What happens when the environment consistently makes the wrong behaviour easier than the right one? If people repeatedly experience an environment where ethical behaviour is punished and unethical behaviour is rewarded, the environment itself becomes part of their leadership development. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. entertainment.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. entertainment.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
entertainment.description: Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U . Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State . Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller , leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections. Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. The Longhorns' march deep into LSU territory concluded with a second-and-goal at the LSU four-yard line with two seconds remaining. Manning took a shotgun snap, dropped back, then lofted a pass to running back Raleek Brown down the right sideline. Brown hauled in the pass. Texas took the lead, then escaped Baton Rougue with a clutch comeback victory on the subsequent kickoff. Arch Manning and Raleek Brown with the biggest play of their careers. sports.title: Islanders, Holmstrom tear through Ducks defense, 6-2
sports.description: Anaheim, CA - New York Islanders right wing Simon Holmstrom (92) and center Kyle Palmieri (21) celebrate after a second period goal during a regular season NHL game between the New York Islanders and the Anaheim Ducks at Honda Center on November 14, 2026, in Anaheim, CA. ANAHEIM, Calif. – That lightning hot offensive streak of a week ago papered over plenty of the Anaheim Ducks’ defensive cracks, which have suddenly morphed into canyons as the goals have dried up. The New York Islanders scored four in the second period through a porous Ducks defense, and Simon Holmström finished off a hat trick past Lukáš Dostál, as Anaheim was cratered, 6-2, on Saturday at Honda Center. Anaheim (10-9-1, 21 points) has scored just four goals in back-to-back losses after scoring 26 goals in a five-game winning streak and five or more goals in eight straight games. Nikita Nesterenko chased down a loose puck in front for the Ducks’ opening goal in the second period, 2-1, and Cutter Gauthier continued his historic goal-scoring streak later in the middle frame. Gauthier carved out space alone in front, and Tristan Luneau sent in the hard feed for the deflection, 5-2. Gauthier tied 1998-99 Teemu Selanne for the second-longest goal-scoring streak in franchise history. Selanne also owns the longest streak in team history at 11 games (1997-98). Ben Hutton was the beneficiary of a double deflection off Ducks sticks just under two minutes into the game, but the Islanders were off to the race in the second period, as wheels came off for Anaheim’s defense. Bo Horvat netted a one-timer six seconds into the first power play of the game, 2-0. Simon Holmstrom scored his first of two 25 seconds after the Ducks’ first goal from Nesterenko, as he finished a two-on-one with Matthew Schaefer. Holmstrom scored a second five minutes later, as Dostál was slid into by Leo Carlsson, and Mitchell Chaffee put in the Islanders’ fifth, as Schaefer flew the zone for another two-on-one. Holmstrom finished off the hat trick with a one-on-one beat of Dostál’s glove in the third period, 6-2. Lukáš Dostál stopped 19 of 25 shots in his first start in over a week, when he was pulled after the first period in Calgary last Friday. Ville Husso was the back-up, as Laurent Brossoit was reassigned back to AHL San Diego yesterday. Brossoit–who won his first four starts of the five he made with the Ducks during their red hot offensive streak–was the only goalie waiver exempt, and thus he was not at risk for a claim by another team when being sent to the minors. Semyon Varlamov made 26 saves for the Islanders. Anaheim concludes its four-game homestand with the second half of a back-to-back against the Calgary Flames on Sunday before hitting the road for a four-game trip, which begins in St. Louis on Tuesday.

sports.title: Steve Sarkisian dials up game-winning TD pass to Raleek Brown
sports.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Running back Raleek Brown #0 of the Texas Longhorns celebrates his touchdown during the game between Louisiana State Tigers and Texas Longhorns at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Aric Becker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images In high-profile calls on the goal line over the last several seasons, Steve Sarkisian has come up short in tenure-defining moments. On Saturday in Baton Rouge, facing off against longtime friend and former colleague Lane Kiffin, Sarkisian faced a season-defining moment hoping to make a better call than he has in the past with six seconds remaining and Texas trailing 21-16 at the LSU 4-yard line. With no timeouts remaining, the Longhorns had no more than two plays remaining. After LSU took away some of the play calls that Sarkisian went back to over the previous two games, a condensed formation created leverage to the field with return motion from running back Raleek Brown creating a clear pre-snap picture for Arch Manning. Trying to match up with Brown in coverage, LSU linebacker Davohn Keys was slow to respond to the return motion, had to take a wide angle around the field corner, and got torched, allowing Manning to hit a one-step drop and drop an easy pass into Brown’s chest for the go-ahead, four-yard touchdown with four seconds remaining. GIVE SARKISIAN HIS CREDIT RALEEK BROWN 1 ON 1 SCORES THE LIKELY GAME-WINNING TD pic.twitter.com/tpBW0Monsp — Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 15, 2026 The Tigers were able to take away Brown in the passing game before the final offensive play for the Horns — Brown only had three catches for four yards on his first four targets, but pitting his speed to the pylon against a slower linebacker who had to navigate traffic ultimately represented one of Sarkisian’s best goal-line play calls in his nearly six years leading the Longhorns. Manning ran to embrace the head coach who trusted him in his lowest moment as an athlete, but it wasn’t a moment to celebrate for the Texas head coach. Up 22-21, Sarkisian had to call a kneel down instead of attempting a point after the Tigers could return for a go-ahead score, and the Longhorns secured the victory on the ensuing kickoff. Reflecting on the play, Brown knew it was won before the snap when a defender didn’t follow him in motion . “I was just real happy,” Brown said . ”Whatever it takes to win.” For Texas, that’s required effective play calls from Sarkisian on the goal line in defining moments. On Saturday, he got it right with one of the single best decisions in his Longhorns tenure.

sports.title: MSU football grades for the Spartans' performance against Washington
sports.description: Lansing State Journal columnist Graham Couch grades Michigan State's football team after its 21-14 loss to Washington on a scale of 1-10. OFFENSE: 3 This grade should probably be an incomplete. Because MSU’s offense was doing well enough before quarterback Alessio Milivojevic went down in the second quarter with an injury. He was 7-for-12 passing for 108 yards and led a touchdown drive to open the game, which including a 30-yard pass to Bryson Williams and a 26-yard completion to Carson Gulker. Without Milivojevic, MSU had some moments offensively with backup Cam Fancher — including a fourth-down touchdown pass to Williams — but also had some moments Fancher and the Spartans would like to have back, including when he threw an interception as he tried to throw away a pass, also injuring himself on the play as he tried to twist out of a tackle. MSU ran the ball somewhat effectively, with Brandon Tullis carrying 21 times again for 82 yards. And, overall, out-gained Washington 342 yards to 332. There were times when this was an effective offense, especially with Milivojevic under center. But the penalties, inconsistencies and turnovers left the Spartans sitting at 14 points, which wasn’t enough. DEFENSE: 7 Once MSU’s defense got a handle on Washington, that was it for the Huskies for a long time. Early on, the Spartans looked like they might get gashed all night by quarterback Demond Williams Jr. and receiver Chris Lawson. But after the Huskies’ second touchdown, MSU’s defense pressured Williams and largely contained everything Washington tried to do, holding the Huskies to 41 total yards on their first four second-half drives. The Spartans only recorded one sack — Williams is elusive and good as stepping up and through pressure to gain a couple yards — but if you watched the game, you saw the work that was being done to corral him. Washington also was only able to rush for 44 yards on 22 carries. In the end, MSU’s defense needed at least one more stop and gave up a few plays on the final drive that beat them. But this was a strong effort — and could have been a winning effort. This grade would be even better if not for those two early drives and for Kenny Soares Jr.'s roughing the passer penalty, which let Washington’s first drive continue, ending in a touchdown. This might have been a different game without that drive. SPECIAL TEAMS: 5 Liam Boyd missed his only field goal attempt, wide right from 50 yards out, and that might have been costly. He definitely could have given the Spartans the lead early in the fourth quarter with that kick. Rhys Dakin’s punting average, 39.6, was impacted by one kick especially when he was punting with a short field and trying to pin Washington deep. He got it to the 13-yard line. Not a great punt, but decent enough. Overall, he had three punts inside the 20-yard line. And Washington’s return man muffed one of his punts, with the Spartans’ coverage unit jumping on it. Chrishon McCray had one nice, 16-yard punt return.

sports.title: ‘Karma’ – Fans react to Lane Kiffin seemingly crying after LSU’s season-ruining loss to Texas
sports.description: Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin’s emotional moment on the field after their 22-21 loss to the Texas Longhorns ended any hopes of making it to the College Football Playoffs. Kiffin coached Ole Miss to the playoff last season but did not get to see the season through after being asked to leave the program for agreeing midseason to join LSU in 2026, a decision that has kept him more unpopular than ever among casual fans. sports.title: Hopewell’s TreVeyon Henderson placed on injured reserve by Patriots
sports.description: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson was placed on injured reserve Nov. 14 by the team as the former Hopewell High School star battles unexplained neurological symptoms that hospitalized him. The move means that Henderson, who has not played in a game since Oct. 22, is guaranteed to miss the next four weeks. He will be re-evaluated later to determine whether he will be done for the season. The Patriots, who are in Munich, Germany this weekend for a game against the Detroit Lions, listed the reason as “illness” for Henderson’s placement on IR. No timetable was given for his return. If cleared to play, the earliest Henderson could return to the field would be Dec. 21 for a home game against the Buffalo Bills . Henderson announced his condition in a post on his X account, saying he had been hospitalized after suffering an unknown neurological episode. Neither he nor the team has confirmed if Henderson remains in the hospital as his X post asked for privacy. Henderson starred at Hopewell High School where he led the Blue Devils to the 2019 state championship. A highly sought-after recruit, he signed with Ohio State and was part of the Buckeyes’ 2024 national championship team. He was drafted in the second round by the Patriots in 2025. In Henderson’s rookie season, he rushed for 911 yards and nine touchdowns, and the Patriots reached Super Bowl XL. Before illness sidelined him, Henderson had rushed 52 times for 203 yards and one touchdown this season. science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans.
